```plato

    //==
    // # Ortho, meta and gyro on polygon meshes
    //
    // The three Conway operators that subdivide every face without moving any
    // original vertex (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway_polyhedron_notation):
    //
    //   ortho   one quad per CORNER          (o = jj = de)
    //   meta    two triangles per CORNER     (m = kj = db)
    //   gyro    one pentagon per CORNER      (g = ds, chiral)
    //
    // Ortho and meta share one vertex block — the original vertices, then the
    // edge midpoints in undirected-edge order, then the face centroids — which is
    // the same three-block layout Catmull-Clark uses, and the reason ortho is the
    // topology of one Catmull-Clark step. Gyro needs the one-third points along
    // each directed edge instead of the midpoints, which is `TruncationPoints`
    // reused unchanged.
    //
    // Preconditions as above. None of the three normalizes its result.

    //==
    // Ortho and meta.

    // Original vertices, then one vertex per undirected edge, then one per face.
    SubdividedVertices(self: PolygonMesh3D): Array<Point3D>
        => Concatenate(
            Concatenate(self.Positions, self.UndirectedEdgeMidpoints),
            self.FaceCentroids);

    // A corner's edge midpoint, read as a vertex of `SubdividedVertices`.
    EdgeMidVertex(self: PolygonMesh3D, corner: CornerIndex): VertexIndex
        => VertexIndex(self.VertexCount + self.CornerUndirectedEdge(corner).Value);

    // A corner's face centroid, read as a vertex of `SubdividedVertices`.
    FaceCentroidVertex(self: PolygonMesh3D, corner: CornerIndex): VertexIndex
        => VertexIndex(self.VertexCount + self.UndirectedEdgeCount + self.CornerFace(corner).Value);

    // The quad a corner contributes to an ortho: its own edge midpoint, the
    // vertex the corner points at, the next edge's midpoint, and the centroid.
    OrthoFaceOfCorner(self: PolygonMesh3D, corner: CornerIndex): Array<VertexIndex>
        => [self.EdgeMidVertex(corner),
            self.CornerDestination(corner),
            self.EdgeMidVertex(self.NextCorner(corner)),
            self.FaceCentroidVertex(corner)];

    // Ortho (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway_polyhedron_notation): every
    // n-gon becomes n quadrilaterals. Cube -> the topology of a subdivided cube,
    // dodecahedron -> the pentagonal-quad form. o = jj = de.
    // V' = V + E + F, E' = 4E, F' = C.
    Ortho(self: PolygonMesh3D): PolygonMesh3D
        => PolygonMeshOfFaces(
            self.SubdividedVertices,
            self.CornerCount.MapRange(c => self.OrthoFaceOfCorner(CornerIndex(c))));

    // The half of a corner nearer its own vertex: vertex, edge midpoint, centroid.
    MetaFirstFaceOfCorner(self: PolygonMesh3D, corner: CornerIndex): Array<VertexIndex>
        => [self.CornerVertex(corner),
            self.EdgeMidVertex(corner),
            self.FaceCentroidVertex(corner)];

    // The far half: edge midpoint, the vertex the corner points at, centroid.
    MetaSecondFaceOfCorner(self: PolygonMesh3D, corner: CornerIndex): Array<VertexIndex>
        => [self.EdgeMidVertex(corner),
            self.CornerDestination(corner),
            self.FaceCentroidVertex(corner)];

    // Meta (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway_polyhedron_notation): every
    // n-gon becomes 2n triangles — the barycentric subdivision of the surface,
    // and the finest of the operators that keeps every original vertex. m = kj = db.
    // V' = V + E + F, E' = 6E, F' = 2C.
    Meta(self: PolygonMesh3D): PolygonMesh3D
        => PolygonMeshOfFaces(
            self.SubdividedVertices,
            Concatenate(
                self.CornerCount.MapRange(c => self.MetaFirstFaceOfCorner(CornerIndex(c))),
                self.CornerCount.MapRange(c => self.MetaSecondFaceOfCorner(CornerIndex(c)))));

    //==
    // Gyro.

    // The one-third points along every directed edge, then the original
    // vertices, then the face centroids. The corner block comes first so a
    // corner number IS its own vertex number, as in truncate.
    GyroVertices(self: PolygonMesh3D): Array<Point3D>
        => Concatenate(
            Concatenate(self.TruncationPoints, self.Positions),
            self.FaceCentroids);

    // An original vertex, read as a vertex of `GyroVertices`.
    GyroSeedVertex(self: PolygonMesh3D, vertex: VertexIndex): VertexIndex
        => VertexIndex(self.CornerCount + vertex.Value);

    // A face centroid, read as a vertex of `GyroVertices`.
    GyroCentroidVertex(self: PolygonMesh3D, face: FaceIndex): VertexIndex
        => VertexIndex(self.CornerCount + self.VertexCount + face.Value);

    // The pentagon a corner contributes: the face centroid, this corner's
    // one-third point, its twin's (the two-thirds point of the same edge), the
    // vertex the corner points at, and the next corner's one-third point. The
    // twin's point is what makes gyro CHIRAL — swapping it for the previous
    // corner's gives the mirror operator.
    GyroFaceOfCorner(self: PolygonMesh3D, corner: CornerIndex): Array<VertexIndex>
        => [self.GyroCentroidVertex(self.CornerFace(corner)),
            VertexIndex(corner.Value),
            VertexIndex(self.TwinCorner(corner).Value),
            self.GyroSeedVertex(self.CornerDestination(corner)),
            VertexIndex(self.NextCorner(corner).Value)];

    // Gyro (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway_polyhedron_notation): every
    // n-gon becomes n pentagons. It is the dual of snub (g = ds), so gT is the
    // pentagonal icositetrahedron's tetrahedral cousin and gD the pentagonal
    // hexecontahedron's family. Chiral, like snub.
    // V' = V + 2E + F, E' = 5E, F' = C.
    Gyro(self: PolygonMesh3D): PolygonMesh3D
        => PolygonMeshOfFaces(
            self.GyroVertices,
            self.CornerCount.MapRange(c => self.GyroFaceOfCorner(CornerIndex(c))));

    //==
    // # Chamfer, propeller, zip and reflect on polygon meshes
    //
    // The last operators of the catalog
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway_polyhedron_notation), plus the mirror
    // that makes the chiral ones legible:
    //
    //   chamfer    one hexagon per EDGE, faces kept parallel   (c)
    //   propeller  one rotated n-gon per face + one quad per CORNER (p, chiral)
    //   zip        the Conway identity z = dk, i.e. truncate of the dual
    //   reflect    the mirror image, with every face loop reversed (r)
    //
    // Chamfer reuses `TwistedFacePoints` at zero twist — the same shrunk corner
    // block expand is built from — but keeps the ORIGINAL vertices as well, which
    // is what leaves the seed's faces parallel to where they started rather than
    // pulled apart. Propeller reuses `TruncationPoints`, the one-third points gyro
    // and truncate already share.

    //==
    // Chamfer.

    // The shrunk corner points, then the original vertices.
    ChamferVertices(self: PolygonMesh3D, shrink: Number): Array<Point3D>
        => Concatenate(self.TwistedFacePoints(shrink, Angle(0.0)), self.Positions);

    // An original vertex, read as a vertex of `ChamferVertices`.
    ChamferSeedVertex(self: PolygonMesh3D, vertex: VertexIndex): VertexIndex
        => VertexIndex(self.CornerCount + vertex.Value);
```
